features.headline: How does Jessie Bates III help the Jaguars defense? Are Falcons still contending?
features.desc: The Falcons decided it was wiser to get something for Bates now rather than letting him walk in free agency.
features.by: Michael DiRocco and Marc Raimondi and Jordan Reid
body: JACKSONVILLE, Fla. — The Jacksonville Jaguars addressed one of their biggest weaknesses Monday by sending a 2027 second-round draft pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick to the Atlanta Falcons for safety Jessie Bates III.
This was the first move the team made before Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET trade deadline to try and solidify itself as a legitimate contender.

The Jaguars also traded a conditional 2028 sixth-round pick for New Orleans Saints DT Davon Godchaux, according to NFL Network's Cameron Wolfe, after losing nose tackle DaVon Hamilton for the rest of the season with a quad injury.
At 6-2, the Jaguars are in third place in the AFC and have a three-game lead in the AFC South. These moves could suggest a win-now mentality.
Bates, who made the Pro Bowl in 2023, can stabilize a secondary that has been hit with multiple injuries at safety and cornerback.

The Jaguars made a similar move last season at the trade deadline by acquiring receiver Jakobi Meyers to help a position group that had multiple players out with injuries and that keyed an offensive surge that carried them to a division title.
The hope is that Bates can do the same for the secondary because getting through the AFC means beating some of the league's top QBs — especially Buffalo's Josh Allen.
The Falcons, on the other hand, were able to get good draft capital for a player on an expiring contract but are still competing in the NFC South.
What does this move mean for the Jaguars' defense and the Falcons' draft plans? ESPN NFL Nation reporters Michael DiRocco and Marc Raimondi and NFL draft analyst Jordan Reid take a look at each.

features.headline: Why the Raiders are better off standing pat at the NFL trade deadline
features.desc: The NFL trade deadline is on Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET. Have Kubiak, Raiders given hints that they might not make moves?
body: SANTA CLARA, Calif. — Coach Klint Kubiak said his calculations of the Las Vegas Raiders change weekly.

In the Raiders' 38-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday afternoon, during which they committed five turnovers on six possessions in the second half, Kubiak saw a team that can be close to competing with the best, but doesn't have enough talent to close that gap.
With the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET, the Raiders sit at 4-5 and are mathematically still in the playoff hunt.
At the same time, they are not in a position to be aggressive and make a big deal for a wide receiver or interior defensive lineman — two positions of significant need.

Meanwhile, the list of players they could trade to obtain draft capital is fairly thin. Of course, there's Maxx Crosby, but the team is not expected to move him, and the star defensive end said he wants to be with the organization for a "long time."
To that end, the Raiders are better off standing pat and pushing through the remainder of the season with the roster as is.

"I really like our team," Kubiak said. "I don't like losing games like this. We've got to have a lot more resilience when you're playing a really good team like we played today. When you start that slow, you don't put yourself in a good position, but I'm proud to coach the guys that we're coaching."
To some degree, the Raiders might've exceeded expectations by starting 3-0 and posting a.500 record through eight weeks, the first time since 2021.
Going into the season, Las Vegas wanted to be competitive, which is why they spent big during free agency. Nonetheless, the Raiders are not oblivious to the organization's current state.

features.headline: 'The World Cup never really ended': U.S.-based betting sees rise in wagering on MLS, European soccer
features.desc: Before the World Cup, many wondered if Americans would stick around afterward. Betting data says yes, they did.
body: Soccer was the sport of the summer in the United States this year, as the FIFA World Cup came to 11 American cities (in addition to venues in Canada and Mexico).
Americans embraced the sport fully, supporting tremendous numbers for television viewership and stadium attendance — as well as sports betting handle.
BetMGM said that the World Cup "nearly kept pace with the MLB's rigorous summer schedule" despite there being five times as many baseball games over that time period.

Hard Rock Bet noted the tournament did three times as much handle and brought in double the number of individual bettors as the men's NCAA tournament, which is traditionally the most-bet-on event on the U.S. sports calendar.

In Colorado, which breaks down betting revenue by sport, the World Cup generated $60.2 million, a near 250% increase from the $17.5 million brought in by the previous edition of the tournament in November 2022.
With European league soccer in full swing and Major League Soccer kicking off playoffs, that momentum has continued over for the American sports betting ecosystem.

BetMGM noted that in the two-month period immediately following the conclusion of the 2026 World Cup, the sportsbook saw a 24.5% year-over-year increase in bets and a 34.5% increase in handle on wagers for club soccer.

Hard Rock said there have been nearly 30% more wagers on soccer overall, specifically 43% more in the Premier League and 21% in the Champions League with World Cup stars Kylian Mbappé, Erling Haaland and Harry Kane attracting double the amount of bets in the competition compared to the same time period last year.

features.headline: As the 'Peanut Punch' takes over NFL, how do teams counter it?
features.desc: After Charles Tillman popularized the punch 14 years ago, it has really taken off this season.
body: ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. — On Oct. 11, New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo fumbled away a win. The Giants lined up in field goal range coming out of the two-minute warning in overtime. Any points would have won the game.

Washington Commanders defensive lineman Daron Payne had other thoughts. After Skattebo was hit in the backfield and had to use his forearms to shed a tackle, he couldn't get the ball back up to his chest.
Payne threw his blocker out of the way and threw his fist at the daylight between Skattebo and the football. Ball out. The Giants' chance at a win was erased, and the game ended in a tie.
Payne executed an increasingly popular — and violent — maneuver called the "Peanut Punch,"

wherein a would-be tackler throws a haymaker at the football in an attempt to pop it loose rather than wrapping up the ball carrier — a technique popularized around 2012 and named after former Chicago Bears defender Charles "Peanut" Tillman.
One day later, Buffalo Bills running back James Cook III fell victim to the same fate.

Carrying from the Los Angeles Rams' 22-yard line early in overtime, Cook squeezed the ball low, around the left side of his abdomen. Had Cook had the ball higher, the incoming punch from linebacker Nate Landman might have left a bruise, but the ball wouldn't have had anywhere to go.

With the ball at Cook's side, Landman found a crease between Cook's armpit and wrist and wedged the ball through. Ball out. Rams possession. Had it not been for a blocked field goal minutes later, Cook's fumble would've meant Bills defeat.

features.headline: What's fueling the rocky start for Giannis Antetokounmpo and the Miami Heat
features.desc: At 4-6, the Heat aren't pointing fingers — yet. But with each loss, the pressure rises on this season and next — with Giannis' free agency looming.
body: IF THE NIGHT had ended differently, Klay Thompson would have had a very different agenda for his off day in Los Angeles. There had been talk of a visit to Catalina Island and extended visits with friends and family in his hometown.
But those plans evaporated quickly after the Miami Heat gave up a staggering 138 points in a loss to the Los Angeles Lakers last Monday.
It was Miami's fourth game of its first seven in which the defense had given up 125 or more points — and it could've been worse. The Lakers had scored 79 points in the first half.

"It's important for all of us to stay present and not look too far ahead in the season," Thompson told ESPN. "When you have big expectations, you think about the postseason, you think about seeding. I think we just need to really stay week-to-week.
"That's the true joy when you build a great team. It's just the beginning stages, and then you see it jell."

The five-time All-Star won four NBA championships with the Golden State Warriors and said he still believes in what this Heat team can become just as much as he did when he gave up millions of dollars in a contract buyout with the Dallas Mavericks to join Miami this summer to play alongside superstar forward Giannis Antetokounmpo, who was acquired in a blockbuster trade with the Milwaukee Bucks in June.

"That Heat culture is real," Thompson said. "I just love the intensity and competitiveness from everyone in this organization. Mr. Riley, Coach. My dad [Mychal Thompson] played for Mr. Riley [with the Lakers], so this is a pretty full-circle moment for us."

features.headline: Who will win MVP? Cy Young? Picks, analysis for 2026 MLB awards week
features.desc: Baseball's best players and managers of 2026 collect their hardware this week — starting tonight with the year's top rookies.
body: The baseball offseason has felt pretty normal so far, at least if you can put the overhanging labor negotiations out of your mind.
Some of that normalcy comes from the gradual easing into the initial phases of the hot stove season — contract options, roster maneuvering, free agency filing — that point toward next season.
That's administrative stuff, though, and not as fun as the parade in Milwaukee, or this week, when MLB hands out its major awards in what more or less closes the books on the 2026 season.

This year's awards week is an expansion of the usual routine because we have a new honor being handed out by the Baseball Writers' Association of America: the Reliever of the Year Award, which recognizes the top bullpen maestro from each league. Here's how this week's schedule lays out:

Monday: Rookie of the Year (7 p.m. ET, MLB Network) Tuesday: Manager of the Year (7 p.m. ET, MLB Network) Wednesday: Cy Young and Reliever of the Year (7 p.m. ET, MLB Network) Thursday: MVP (7 p.m. ET, MLB Network)
MLB Network will also air the MLB awards given out during a live ceremony in Las Vegas at 8 p.m. ET on Wednesday.

Honors given out then include the Hank Aaron Award, Comeback Player of the Year, Mariano Rivera & Trevor Hoffman Relievers of the Year, Edgar Martinez Outstanding Designated Hitter Award and selections for the All-MLB first and second teams.
Finalists for the major awards have already been announced. So let's see how things look before the hardware is handed out. Who might win? Who should win?
